items.note: Neither the Alpha 1-4/2-4 LSCbasic operating manual (Rev. 2.2), the product pages, nor the 2024 LSCbasic brochure states a time for the ice condenser to cool from room temperature to its approx. -55 C operating temperature. The manual only says the condenser is pre-cooled ('cool-down') during the 15 min vacuum-pump warm-up and says to switch on 20 to 30 min before drying. That is a pump warm-up instruction, not a cooldown specification, so it is not reported.

Same documents as the Alpha 1-4. No cooldown time is stated for the -85 C ice condenser of the Alpha 2-4 LSCbasic. The manual's 20 to 30 min switch-on lead time is for vacuum-pump warm-up, not a documented condenser cooldown.

The Martin Christ Pilot Freeze Dryers brochure (EN 10/2017) gives only a shelf cooling/heating rate (> 1 K/min, +20 C to -40 C) and the condenser temperature (-85 C). It states no time from room temperature to operating temperature. A rate is not a cooldown time, and no value was derived from it.

The Pilot Freeze Dryers brochure (EN 10/2017) gives only a shelf cooling/heating rate (> 2 K/min, +20 C to -40 C) and the condenser temperature (-88 C). It states no cooldown or pull-down time to operating temperature.

The Pilot Freeze Dryers brochure (EN 10/2017) gives only a shelf cooling/heating rate (> 1 K/min, +20 C to -40 C) for the Epsilon 2-6D/2-10D/2-12D/2-16D and the condenser temperature (-85 C). It states no cooldown time.

The Memmert TT300E75 technical data page lists the range (-75 to +180 C), the water-cooled condenser and the shelves, but no cooling rate and no pull-down time to -75 C. The TESTA brochure on a distributor site could not be snapshotted because it returned a security-check page. Distributor text mentions up to 10 K/min for the TESTA line, but not for this model and not as a pull-down time.

The MI 6800C brochure and product page say only that the system can be 'operational within several hours' from mains power, which gives no number. The '2 hours from room temperature sample change to 3He condensation temperature' Initial Cooldown Time belongs to the optional He-3 insert, which this configuration does not include. The '10 minutes with VTI cold' figure is a sample cooldown that assumes the system is already cold. Neither is the system cooldown from room temperature.

In this configuration samples sit in a passive 3.2 L LN2 analysis dewar that the user fills (77 K, >70 h hold). There is no refrigerator to cool down. The brochure's 60 minute 'Cool Down Time to Stated Minimum from Ambient' applies only to the Cryostat I GM accessory (configuration micromeritics_3flex_cryostat_i), not to the LN2 dewar.

The Minitube IceCube 14M/14S leaflet (V1 09/2025) and the 14M-A catalog page give the temperature range (+40 to -180 C) and the cooling rates (0.01 to 60 C/min), but no time to pre-cool the chamber to the start temperature. The program start temperature is user-variable. No value was derived from the rate.
Same leaflet as the 14M. It states no chamber pre-cool or pull-down time for the IceCube 14S, only cooling rates of 0.01 to 60 C/min.

The DHS SAVER RID market survey (09/2015) gives no Falcon 5000 cooldown. It states only a generic '30 minutes or more' for HPGe RIDs in general, which is not model-specific. The Mirion Falcon 5000 training PDF and the spectroscopy catalog are blocked by robots.txt and could not be snapshotted. The Mirion 2021 portable-HPGe presentation gives '<12 hours' for the Aegis cryocooler, which is a different product.

items.quote: Cool down time ~2 hours to 4.2 K
items.document_title: CryoAdvance-50 Fully automated, closed-cycle optical cryostat (Montana Instruments datasheet, Quantum Design GmbH)
items.note: The manufacturer datasheet gives an approximate time (~2 h) to 4.2 K. The configuration's base temperature is 3.2 K, so the time to full base may be slightly longer. 4.2 K is the only documented cooldown endpoint.
